citations.quote: However, seldom researches focus on integrating DT with MBSE for the SD complexity analysis and prediction. As SD can be viewed as the supply and demand of knowledge between designers and product functions, from a knowledge perspective, this paper firstly introduces a framework for integrating DT with MBSE called System Design Digital Twin in 5 Dimensions (SDDT5D). The frame provides services for design complexity measurement, effort estimation, and change propagation prediction. Then, to represent the system design digital twin in a unified way, a modeling profile is constructed through SysML stereotypes. The system model reduces ambiguity through unifying system requirements, functions, and structures and behaviors. Finally, the SD of a Radio Aurora Explorer mission demonstrates the proposed method.

Through FAST, Fig.2 shows a function tree diagram with 36 functions of SD of a Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) mission. According to FAST's functional decomposition criteria, when a function is simple enough to map to existing or commercially available components or subsystems, the decomposition can stop. For example, "Function 3-Convert solar energy into electricity" in Fig.2 is at the end level as a solar wing can accomplish it.

We use a scale to map a function into knowledge space to evaluate the required knowledge items in designing a specific function. Based on the study by Zhang and Thomson [26], we use knowledge magnitude to indicate the importance of a certain knowledge item to the function development, where a higher value indicates a severer requirement.

The knowledge-based SD in Section2 establishes a theoretical basis for the operation of a system design digital twin. According to the research from Tao, a complete digital twin framework should include five components: the physical entity in physical space, the virtual entity in virtual space, services for analyzing the entity, digital twin data from the entity, and connections between them [30].

System design in the framework (Fig.4) is an iterative optimization process. The system design digital model represents information of design objects, designers, and design activities from the design team. With the development of the system, the digital model information becomes complete. Moreover, through system services, the actual system design process can be optimized.

Stereotypes are used for customizing core concepts of System Design Digital Twin in 5 Dimensions (SDDT $ _{5D} $ ). A $ SDDT_{5D} $ modeling profile is constructed, as displayed in Fig.6, where mappings and decomposition relationships, etc. constitute the relationship profile; the function DT, designer DT, and design activity DT profiles form the $ SDDM_{VS} $ profile. The product data, designer data, and design activity data profiles constitute the DTD profile. The design complexity measurement, effort estimation, and change propagation prediction profiles constitute the SDS profile.

Two kinds of mapping relationships: (a) mapping at the same level and (b) mapping between two different levels, are named as H mapping and V mapping, respectively, by extending the "dependency" relationship.

Additionally, an interface consists of a connector (named Interface_connector) and two ports (named Interface_Port). An Interface_connector extends from the Connector and inherits from the Block; an Interface_Port inherits from the ProxyPort.
SysML supports different types of engineering analyses using parametric models, which capture constraints on the properties of a system and can then be evaluated by an appropriate analysis tool.

Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) is a standard mission in the aerospace field. The primary objective of the mission is to study the formation of magnetic field-aligned plasma irregularities (FAI). Based on a RAX CubeSat project, in 2012, the SSWG (Space Systems Working Group) of INCOSE demonstrated the feasibility of the MBSD approach in reality, where SysML could formally specify every aspect of a system [31]. Accordingly, in the following section, the modeling approach proposed in this paper is applied to the system design of a virtual RAX CubeSat mission.

Necessary information has been given, for example, the decomposed functions are revealed in Fig.2, the required knowledge is provided in Table2, and the interfaces among functions are shown in Fig.11 in [28]. Besides, the quantitative aspects of designers and design activities are required, which are shown in Table6.

TriangularD (40,64,50) is selected as the triangle distribution in the design activity data, and the information receiving and preparation time are set to 2h, respectively. Furthermore, function 16 $ \left( \mathrm{F}_{1 6} \right) $ is the key function because it has the most interfaces, and function 17 $ \left( \mathrm{F}_{1 7} \right) $ is selected as the changed function.

The first step is to specify models and organize them initially. An overall package structure based on the $ \mathrm{SDDT}_{5 \mathrm{D}} $ is used to establish the model organization, as displayed in Fig.15. Thus, different models are organized into specific packages according to the aim of them.

Details of each package are modeled. For example, decomposition of the functions is described by the SysML Block Definition Diagram (BDD) because functions are treated as components that can be "assembled", as illustrated in Fig.16.
Interfaces of the functions are then described by the SysML Internal Block Diagram (IBD), as exhibited in Fig.17.

One function is assigned to one designer and different design activities, as illustrated in Fig.18. Then, design activities are elaborated to show the behavior of every designer by the SysML Sequence Diagram or Activity Diagram using the design activity DT profile.

Based on the assumption and through the system services modeled by the parametric models, values of parameters in equations on design complexity assessment, workload estimation, and function change analysis are specified by linking to corresponding data. Finally, properties of the system design, such as design complexity and effort, can be evaluated by appropriate analysis tools like MATLAB. The output data of the analysis is listed in Table 7.
It can be seen from Table7 that the total complexity (C_Total) is 195, and the total effort (E_Total) is approximately 4819h.

Based on the estimated design effort, managers can use the trade-off analysis by setting SysML models' different values to optimize the design progress. For example, based on the result, managers can more accurately identify the knowledge requirement of functions and designate more capable designers on key functions.

To assess the proposed method's practical usability, two students (Group A) and two experienced managers (Group B) were asked to participate in an experiment about estimating the total effort of the RAX CubeSate system design. The two students having the SysML knowledge background used the proposed unified models to represnt the system design, while the two managers in Group B used a traditional document-based approach, such as the requirements specification by Microsoft Word and the interface definition document by Microsoft Excel, to specify the system design.

The student group spent about 48h in modeling the system model by the $ \mathrm{SDDT}_{5 \mathrm{D}} $ modeling profile and spend 4 more hours in getting the correct total effort. Compared with students, managers in Group B spend less time in specifying the systems, about 24h. However, the two managers used more time, about 10h, in getting the correct total effort as they wasted more time in understanding the ambiguity issues. Although the students spent more time in modeling the system model, they saved more time in analyzing the design complexity.

Additionally, the effort required to develop the key function $ F_{1 6} $ is about 303h, accounting for 6.29% of the total effort, which can prove that this function is one of the core functions. The information transfer effort $ ( E_{tansfer-F16} ) $ required during the development of $ F_{1 6} $ is 60h, and the knowledge consultation effort of it $ ( E_{Consult-F16} ) $ is about 29h.

According to the prediction, the manager can decide whether to change the corresponding design parameters. Moreover, in Table8, the additional effort for changing $ F_{1 7} $ $ (E_{CP-F17}) $ is approximately 419h, which significantly delays the design cycle.

A significant function of the established unified model is that it can simulate different scenarios by conveniently changing different parameters in the SysML parameter diagram, thereby helping the designer to determine critical functions and interfaces in the early design stage.

The primary purpose of these scenarios is to cover many possible examples of function change propagation: addition/deletion of functions, addition/removal of knowledge items, and modification of interfaces. Simulation results show that additional work is required if there are any changes in the design, as shown in Fig.19.
However, designers criticized the intensive manual work required for building a model. In reality, designers were unwilling to spend so much time in creating SysML diagrams.

More importantly, an experienced manager said that they preferred making decisions by referencing similar cases of a previous design or believing their experience. They suggested a few improvement ideas for future work, such as linking the model to available information databases, and building ontologies for common cases to reuse or reference them rather than creating new ones.

Although SysML modeling tools, such as Magicdraw, enable designers to create and document a system model, many designers in China find it unacceptable to spend too much time in learning such a graphical modeling language without appropriate patterns. Besides, it is difficult for the machine to understand the semantics of the SysML diagrams.
